utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. And good morning to you, sir. The affirmation you made still applies. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, during your direct examination at page 9155 of the transcript, in response to some questions which my colleague Ms. Residovic you told the Chamber that it would most probably be a lie to suggest that on Saturday, the 11th of August, 2001, Mr. Ljupco Bliznakovski had attended a meeting at the defence command for the city of Skopje and then had ordered the chief of OVR Cair to reinforce the check-points in OVR Cair. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that Mr. Ljupco Bliznakovski was in Radusa on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you also explained that you and Mr. Bliznakovski usually knew what the other one was working on, right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, usually.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Tell me, are you familiar with all of the details of Mr. Bliznakovski's activities from the 10th to the 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot speak about all details, but I do know of some.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Of some. All right. And so, for example, you don't know whether-- let me rephrase my question. Do you know who Mr. Bliznakovski spoke with on the telephone on the morning of Saturday, 11th August 2001?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who he spoke with. I know that he left for Radusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So it's also possible, isn't it, that Mr. Bliznakovski performed some activities on that morning, Saturday, the 11th, without telling about it, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Tell me, how long does it take to drive from Skopje to Radusa? About half an hour?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there are no military conditions, yes, about. Under such circumstances, then perhaps more.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And if there are, as you put it, military conditions, how long approximately would that drive have been?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radusa is about 25 kilometres away. In that period of time, the first ten kilometres were more or less secure, I believe; and the rest, according to my experience, the movement would have been very slow.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So would it be fair to say that during those times of military conditions, it could have taken an hour to drive from Skopje to Radusa?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you don't look after your security, yes; but if you do, then at least four hours, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Four hours to drive 25 kilometres. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When you're driving on a terrain that could be mined or grounds which is susceptible to ambush.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Even when you're trying to reach your colleagues who are reportedly encircled by Albanian terrorists. You will take four hours to travel those 25 kilometres to assist them?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You testified that Mr. Bliznakovski, together with a special unit, went to Radusa to help the colleagues who were surrounded by terrorists at that time, and you testified that Mr. Bliznakovski tried to extract them. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that testimony and that they were not just surrounded but that there was heavy fighting going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you explained that the situation in Radusa, this heavy fighting, was happening in the course of the whole day and was only by night-fall that the situation became calmer, and that is when Mr. Bliznakovski came back to the premises of the SVR. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, late in the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And at page 9161 of the transcript you said that at -- I'm going to rephrase my question. It's possible, isn't it, that Mr. Bliznakovski, prior to going from Skopje to Radusa on the 11th of August, also had a meeting in the office of army General Sokol Mitrevski, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of this fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I didn't ask you whether you were aware of it. I asked you whether it was possible. Could you answer my question?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And why isn't it possible? Why wasn't it possible?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, my colleague is on her feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my learned friend's questions, I believe are being posed for the third time and they all deal with possibilities. I don't know what sort of an answer the witness can give, given that he provided clear answers to the previous questions. As to ask anything from the domain of possibility, I don't believe it is a proper question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think in the context of the question something quite well directed, not repetitive and reasonable. Carry on, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Let me repeat my question, Mr. Stojanovski. It's possible, isn't it, that Mr. Bliznakovski, prior to going from Skopje to Radusa on the 11th of August, also had a meeting in the office of army general Sokol Mitrevski, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As are many other things which are possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. You also testified that it's -- it's -- you testified that it's not true that Ljupco Bliznakovski would have ordered the head of OVR Cair to increase the number of persons at police check-points for two reasons. Number one you said that Mr. Bliznakovski could not issue orders to the head of the OVR; and, number two, you said that check-points were under the competence of the OVRs. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you also said: "So I don't see a reason why someone would say this." Why someone would make such an assertion. Now, you recall there was this mine explosion on the 10th of August, 2001, in the territory of OVR Cair at a place called Ljubotenski Bacila, right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Eight Macedonian soldiers were killed and others were wounded. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And members of the Ministry of Interior had strong suspicions at that time that the perpetrators of this act were members of the NLA. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that there were information that the perpetrators of this act moved towards Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's not my question, Mr. Stojanovski. I want you to answer the question that I asked you. The question is: Members of the Ministry of Interior had strong suspicions at that time that the persons who planted the mine that killed eight Macedonian soldiers were members of the NLA, right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we had such information available.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And so at that time the security situation in OVR Cair was very complex, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Wouldn't that be a pretty good reason to suggest or to order that the numbers of police officers at check-points be increased?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the obligation of the head of the OVR Cair.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's interesting, but you did not answer my question again. I'll repeat my question. Wouldn't that be a pretty good reason to suggest or to order that the numbers of police officers at check-points be increased?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The head of OVR Cair could have thought in this manner, or he could have been thinking that the number of police officers engaged at the check-points was sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Wouldn't that be a pretty good reason for someone like Mr. Bliznakovski, someone working in the headquarters of SVR Skopje to suggest or to order that the number of police officers at check-points be increased?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There could be different opinions, but I will say once again, this would be the work of the head of the OVR Cair.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like to go on to another topic, please. At page 9159 of the transcript, in response to a question from Ms. Residovic, you were asked about a telephone call that the head of OVR Cair, Mr. Krstevski, made to you on the 12th of August, 2001; that was Sunday. And you explained that Mr. Krstevski had called you because the duty centre had told Mr. Krstevski that Minister Boskoski was going to come to OVR Cair. And Mr. Krstevski asked you about how this official report is given. And you told the Trial Chamber: "This was rather funny, because, as civilian structures, we don't deal with this issue. Reporting is not part of the tasks which we have or the way we act. I suggested to him that, according to my view, it is quite sufficient that he present a brief information about the situation in the area." Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Help us understand, please. Why do you say that reporting is not part of the tasks of members of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, or the way that members of the Ministry of Internal Affairs act?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The term "to report," is not a mere report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, can you explain your answer a little bit more, please. What do you mean by "the term 'to report,' is not a mere report"?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This report is a military term and it's usually used in military units. The manner is which a report is given. According to my recollection, when I was in the army about 30 years ago, it presumes a procedure, and it could not be compared with briefing which, as you said, is one of the obligations of the MOI employees.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So I'm trying to understand now your testimony. Your testimony is that it's not the obligation or the tasks of MOI employees to report about information, but it is the obligation of MOI employees to brief their superiors about information. Is that your testimony? Is that -- do I have that clear?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The term "report," denotes a specific manner of coming on report and briefing; while report in a civilian structure does not denote these special military procedures or rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Are you aware, Mr. Stojanovski, of an obligatory instruction of the Ministry of Internal Affairs that says all authorised officials are obliged to submit operative information to their superiors?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And all authorised officials are supposed to follow this instruction, right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when authorised officials submit operative information to their superiors, that's one way in which they report to their superiors, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is one way. But I don't see how you are linking this with coming to report. I don't know whether the interpretation is adequate.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, I'm simply trying to understand your testimony, Mr. Stojanovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Perhaps we can show the witness what is Exhibit P178, 00178, and this would be at tab 10 of the Prosecution's binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Maybe before we look at this -- at this document, Mr. Stojanovski, just so I'm sure that I understand your testimony, are you suggesting that when a high-ranking member of the Ministry of Internal Affairs comes to, for example, the territory of the an OVR, it is not the practice of the head of the OVR or other members of the OVR to report to that official about events going on?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He informs them about the current situation and the forces engaged, but he does not go on report. I don't know how else I can explain this term "report." This is not the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you are referring to a specific military procedure. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Just a minute, please, Ms. Residovic. Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: My question was: When you say "he does not go on report," you're referring to a specific military procedure. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The term "reporting," denotes a military procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I wanted to point out an interpretation matter. It seems that the terms in English and Macedonian are not fully equal. In Macedonian can you see that it says operational information, whereas in English we have operational report, or operative report. It is possible that this creates a degree of confusion with the Prosecutor. I'm not trying to interfere with his questions or the witness's answers. I just wanted to point out this may not be the best example because the word "informatica" has been translated as "report."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm grateful to Ms. Residovic for clarifying that because obviously I don't have her linguistic skills. However, and I will accept, I will readily accept her correction to the English translation. But if you allow me, I would just like to continue to ask a question or two about this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please do so, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you take a look at this document, Mr. Stojanovski, It's dated 5th of August, 2001, and it says: operative information. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And the subject is: More inhabitants are moving out. It is submitted by apparently a member of the Ministry of Internal Affairs named Bobi Hristovski. And Mr. Hristovski explains in the first paragraph how, on the 5th of August, 2001, he sees a large number of persons leaving Ljuboten village and going towards Skopje and -- do you see that? A large number of women and children?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The person you mentioned submitted it, an employee at the police station Cair and OVR Cair and this is information containing information which you just spoke about.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if you look at paragraph 2, Officer Hristovski says, "I shall continue to gather useful information and inform the service promptly." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So it's true, isn't it, that it is part of the task, the tasks of members of the Ministry of Internal Affairs to gather useful information on the territory or place where they are working and inform their superiors about it, right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never said this was an issue, outstanding issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm asking you the question, and I'd like to you answer my question, just yes or no. Can you answer my question yes or no?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. If you could turn, please, to what is tab 13 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, this would be Exhibit P00159, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is an Official Note number 1185. It's dated the 11th of August, 2001. And what this Official Note says that an authorised officer named Goran Tenovski, who was at the Ljubanci check-point informed his colleagues i in particular an officer named Venco Stanoevski that on the morning of the 11th of August, the army of the Republic of Macedonia opened fire with infantry weapons in the direction of Ljuboten village. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You mentioned that after the events in Ljuboten occurred, a number of people came to speak to you trying to clarify what had happened in Ljuboten. You mentioned -- I believe you mentioned Sofija Galeva, I believe you mentioned Ms. Katica Jovanovska. You may have mentioned some others. Tell me, please, did you tell Mrs. Galeva or Ms. Jovanovska or anyone else looking into the Ljuboten case to speak with this officer Goran Tenovski about what he had observed that weekend?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no authorisation to involve myself in the work of the commission. I was charged with supplying the commission with all the material that they would request from SVR Cair and to put it at their disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You've told us about your 25 years as a police officer, many of those 25 years working in operative matters in the crime police, we've heard testimony in this case that people came to you for assistance in finding more information about what had happened in Ljuboten on the 12th of August. Now, are you really going to tell the Chamber today that you had no authorisation to involve yourself in the work of the commission and so for that reason you would not have given this simple advice, such as, Speak to this authorised official or speak to that authorised official?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you recall what I said previously on the 13th, I believe, it was, in the afternoon, I was informed by Mr. Efremov that a commission was set up by Mr. Boskoski for looking into the events related to the village of Ljuboten. The task which I was charged with was to serve the commission as a liaison person and to assist it to carry out their requests towards SVR Skopje. In these discussions, of course sometimes I pointed them to OVR Cair so as they could carry out their tasks. That is to say, if I was not able to give them the required information or material from the head office of SVR Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. So I'll ask my question again. Did you tell these persons who came to you from the commission or commissions, since you were the liaison person, did you suggest that they speak to, for example, the Officer Goran Tenovski, who is mentioned in this Official Note, or his colleague Venco Stanoevski about what's with going on around the village of Ljuboten on the 10th to 12th August, did you suggest that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't suggested that they talk to Goran Tenovski, but I believe that I referred them to the OVR Cair.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And by referring these persons to the OVR Cair, for example, did you suggest that they speak with police officers who had been manning check-points at OVR Cair on the 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not suggest it. They had their own task and they probably knew best how to perform that task.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And in this case, just so that the record is clear, when you're using the pronoun "they," you're referring to the members of these commissions who came to speak to you, right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And just by the way, this Official Note here that we're looking at, this would be another example of how members of the Ministry of Interior were informing their superiors about events going on in the area where they worked, right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The usual formats are operative information and Official Note.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we could provide the witness with the second binder that was provided by Ms. Residovic during her direct examination. And if we could turn to what is Exhibit P105, P00105 and that exhibit is at tab 88 of that second binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you have -- this -- and, again, I hope my colleague will collect the translation if there's any problems with it. This document is entitled in English, operative information. I -- it is dated the 13th of August, 2001. It's operative information number 1207, submitted by a colleague named Dragan Surlov. And, Mr. Stojanovski, the subject is telephone message, verbal order transmitted. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It says here: "On the 13th of August 2001 at 2230 hours, duty officers Zlate from," I believe, it is the duty operation centre at SVR Skopje "called the Mirkovci police station and stated that there was an order from the police general not to retaliate to provocations and not to misuse the radio connection (only for active misuse) and for all police to be notified of the order. I informed the check-points and patrols as well as receiver Borce Gjorgjievski." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Excuse me, I'm just looking for the right place in my questions. It would be fair to say, then, doesn't it, that the term "Operative Information" would also -- would extend, for example, to the description of orders given, the reception of orders and the dissemination of orders. Would that be fair?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Much more appropriate term, in accordance with our work, is the term "Official Note."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. In this case --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I think Ms. Residovic has a comment to make, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, no comment. The witness offered the approximate translation of the Macedonian original literally translated it is Official Note. However, in English, we say something rather different, operative information.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you for that clarification. I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But, in any event, Mr. Stojanovski, this is the kind of information that is often reported, or informed, transmitted by members of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, operative information is produced when the officer, police officer or the operations officer, has received some information. An Official Note is produced in cases when certain actions were undertaken and a report is produced when certain actions have been undertaken upon a request of the superior officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. But as I -- as I asked, no matter what we call this document, we can call it an Official Note, the point is, this information needed to be communicated to the OVR Cair, Mirkovci police station, and it was communicated, right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That information was communicated, but I see that in the upper right-hand corner there is the date 24 of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes. And that someone signed off on that when he received it.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. So it means that probably that was the date when this document was received by the OVR Cair.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could it also mean that that was the date when this document was filed away in the analytical section of OVR Cair?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The date is 27th of August, 2001. Obviously there is a difference of three days, so after someone received it and only three days later the document was filed away.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So if this document was written on the 13th of August in 2001, but apparently not received until a couple of weeks or ten day, more than that, later in August -- I think I will simply move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, just for your convenience for more examples of -- to use the witness's term, "information" being submitted to part of the Ministry of Interior, you can see tabs 15 to 21 in the Prosecution's binder. These are exhibits P98, P23, under seal, P00108, P00109, P00145, P00259, P00124, and there are also a number of similar examples in the second binder provided by the Defence during direct examination such as exhibit P00160, P0012, P00150, Exhibit 1D145, exhibit 114 under seal, exhibit P00111, and a number of others that are located in that binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Moving on to another topic, Mr. Stojanovski, during your direct examination, you agreed with a proposition put to you by Ms. Residovic. This is at page 9185 of the transcript. That only the investigative judge is able to request data from the forensic medicine institute. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So if a witness testified in this courtroom that he or she spoke to the director of the forensic medicine institute and received information about the persons who died at Ljuboten, that would be a lie?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could discuss it. However, the official document, if I may say so, is in the ownership of the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. So now if I understand your testimony, you're saying that an official document from the forensic institute would be provided to the investigative judge. However, it is certainly possible for members of the Forensic Institute to give verbal information to members of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Although they shouldn't give information about their findings.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when you say "they," who is they?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the employees in the Forensic Institute.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if members of the Ministry of Interior are working on an important case and they go speak to employees of the Forensic Institute, why shouldn't the employees of the Forensic Institute provide verbal information about their findings?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my experience, this should not be proper.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you cite to any law that prohibits such conversation?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, just for your convenience, the testimony that I referred to a bit earlier is at page 8732 and pages 8800 to 8801 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, at page 9189 of the transcript, Ms. Residovic asked you: "After the burial of bodies has occurred, what is required to answer the basic questions as to how and as a result of what the person died?" And you responded: "The only way to ascertain those things that you mentioned was through exhumation and post-mortem." Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Wouldn't speaking to witnesses also permit you to ascertain how a person died?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this specific case, there were no witnesses.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, we had no witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And tell us what specific actions you took, Mr. Stojanovski, to look for witnesses?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The case was in the competence of the OVR Cair, and I believe that I mentioned before that I established contact with representatives of the international organisations. In trying to receive certain information regarding the events.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So just so -- if I understand what you're -- the implication of what you just said, are you -- you're suggesting that representatives of the -- of international organisations prevented you from taking actions to find witnesses to the events in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not permitted to enter the village of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And what other -- what, if any, efforts did you make to speak to persons, members of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, who had participated in the events in Ljuboten on the 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are asking me about me personally, I did not make any efforts to clarify the case. The OVR Cair was working on clarifying the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Related to that, at page 9190 of the transcript, Ms. Residovic showed you Exhibit 1D47, which was -- which is at tab 146 of the Defence binders. And that was a request from the investigative judge to the Ministry of Internal Affairs for more information related to possible exhumations in Ljuboten village. Do you remember that document?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then on the next page of the transcript, Ms. Residovic showed you Exhibit 1D190, which is at tab 146 of the Defence binder, which was the response of OVR Cair to the investigative judge. And you observed that OVR Cair did not fully succeed in providing all of the information requested by the judge. And you explained to the Chamber that the OVR failed to obtain all of the information "primarily because the population of Ljuboten village did not want to cooperate with the police at all." Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we can show the witness what is Exhibit 1D189. This is at tab 99 in what is actually the second Prosecution binder. And, Your Honour, I have good news and bad news. The bad new, I suppose, is that I have another binder of documents to provide you; but the good news is that I'm only going to refer to them. So please do not despair. So we made the binders, and so we decided to distribute them. Ms. Usher, the binder would be actually over here, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you could turn to what is tab 99 in this binder, you should find Exhibit 1D189. And I am praying that the title of this document has been correctly translated into English. I see my colleagues are nodding their heads, so I can relax a little bit. Mr. Stojanovski, you'll see that this is an Official Note, number 736. It's dated the 15th of November, 2001, submitted by a man named Dejan Blazevski. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: At OVR Cair. And the subject is interview with individual Selim from the village of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And Mr. Blazevski tells us that: "On the 15th of November, 2001, an interview was conducted in OVR Cair with the individual Selim from Ljuboten in connection with the events of 12 August 2001 in the village, during which eight individuals died as a result of fighting between the security forces of the Republic of Macedonia and the terrorist groups stationed in the village." Are you following with me?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then it says: "Selim informed us that the following individuals died on 12 August 2001." And then we see a list of eight names, Rami Jusufi, his parents names, Bajrami Sulejman, Bajrami Xhelal, Bajrami Jashari. Brothers and cousins, Bajrami Kadri, Dalip Murati; Qaili Atulla, who died in a hospital on 14 August 2001; and a six-year-old boy, and the name Isni Ali is given. The identity of the persons who died at Ljuboten village on 12 August 2001, that's pretty important information, isn't it.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is an important information that was produced three months after the events at Ljuboten village, so a person came to OVR Cair and wanted to talk to some of -- to one of the colleagues. But also there is something illogical in this information so it should give rise to suspicion, since in the last paragraph it is written that the burial was performed on the same day, so that would mean on the 12th of August, which is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the agenda of that person might be suspicious.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And having said that, though, this is evidence of some cooperation on very important matters from residents of Ljuboten, isn't it, three months after the event. Isn't it?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The quality of cooperation is doubtful.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And what do you base that opinion on?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since that citizen claims that the burial had been performed on the same date. According to our information the burial was carried out a bit later.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you have any information that the person, the eight persons named in this document and identified is incorrect? Persons identified as people who died at Ljuboten on the 12th of August.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember offhand. I need to look at the documents, at the official documents from the identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I will move on. I'd like you to please turn your mind to the events of 12 August, that Sunday, 2001. At page 9164 of the transcript, you said that on 12 August 2001 -- actually, I'm going to stop for a moment. I'd like to go back to that document that is still in front of you, if I can. If I were to tell you that there had been a lot of testimony in this courtroom about persons who died in the village of Ljuboten on the 12th of August, and that the persons name in this document have been identified by witnesses in this case, would that lay any suspicions that you have about that information in this document?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not dispute the names. I disputed the last paragraph in the information.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Okay. So just so the record is clear, the person who provided this information gave some very important, accurate information to members of Ministry of Interior in November 2001, right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Useful information.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. If you can turn your mind to Sunday, the 12th of August, 2001, please, at page 9164 of the transcript you said that on 12 August 2001 you did not go to OVR Cair because: "There was no need for my presence there." Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that I was not in OVR Cair on the 12th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And that's because there was no need for your presence there, right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Why do you say there was no reason for you to go to OVR Cair on the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Connected to my work tasks and competencies there was no reason for me to be at OVR Cair on the 12th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You told the Chamber at page 9161 of the transcript that OVR Cair was not, due to its limited capacities, able to control the situation around Ljuboten that day. That's what you had told the Chamber in response to a question from Ms. Residovic. Tell us, please, were you in your office in Skopje that day?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Either in my office or in the operative headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Tell us, please, what was going on that day in downtown Skopje that was more urgent than the events in OVR Cair?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: My work tasks did not require of me to be present in OVR Cair.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Was there any shooting going on in the city of Skopje that day?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 12th, in the centre of the city?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall such event.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Any crowds of civilians in the centre of the city of Skopje that day, threatening to attack other civilians?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This happened constantly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm asking about the 12th of August.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every day there were civilians, citizens, who protested in front of the assembly of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And every day, were there ethnic Macedonian civilians, threatening to attack ethnic Albanian citizens in Skopje?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: According to your knowledge, did the Macedonian security forces attack a group of ethnic Albanian terrorists in the village of Ljuboten on 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think I previously said that on 12th August police and army points were attacked at which point the army returned fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if I can just go back to my previous question, you said that not every day there were ethnic Macedonian civilians threatening to attack ethnic Albanian citizens in Skopje. How about on that Sunday, the 12th of August? Do you recall whether there was a crowd of ethnic Macedonian civilians in downtown -- in the centre of Skopje threatening to attack ethnic Albanian civilians that day?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the centre of Skopje? I don't remember anything of this kind. This was happening in OVR Cair.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And you explained that -- you said that on the 12th of August police and army points were attacked at which point the army returned fire. To your knowledge, then, was the purpose of the operation at Ljuboten to confront and neutralize terrorists? Was that the purpose of the Ljuboten operation?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the purpose. I know the information which I received from OVR Cair.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, what did the information that you received from OVR Cair tell you about why members of the security forces of the Republic of Macedonia entered Ljuboten on the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not conveyed to me why this -- the army entered Ljuboten on the 12th of August. It was pointed out to me, it was conveyed to me, that the police and army points were attacked, that the security forces returned fire, and that the army undertook an operation of a kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, we have had several witnesses come into this courtroom, take the oath that have you taken, sit in that witness chair and told the Trial Chamber that the members of the army of Macedonia did not enter the village of Ljuboten that day, and we have some documentary evidence to that effect as well. Are you suggesting that each of these witnesses came into this courtroom and lied?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting anything. I am just telling you what I was conveyed by OVR Cair.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you think that the members of the security forces who enter the Ljuboten on the 12th of August were heroes, patriots?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how to -- and what to answer to this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like your opinion. I'd like your belief.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that there were people who were carrying out their duty, but as for whether there were events there which could be qualified as heroic or patriotic, this I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. So you believe that the members of the security forces who entered Ljuboten village on the 12th of August were carrying out their duty, right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is much closer to my view.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And their duty, in your belief, was to protect the territory and the people of the Republic of Macedonia, right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably to establish the sovereignty.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Because the sovereignty of Macedonia was under great threat at that time, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The terrorists were attempting by way of force to put down the constitutional order of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, the persons who died and were -- or were injured at Ljuboten, how would you describe them? Were they terrorists?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible. But this may -- need not be.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. If they were terrorists, these persons were terrorists, do you feel that effectively they got what they deserved?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe that one can put it that way. It would be very rough to put it in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: How would you put it?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably they were aware that taking up arms and attacking of the police and the army would entail certain risks. When someone is going into a fight, one has to be aware of the fact that one might die. When we're talking about who deserves what, this is usually a matter of the courts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And since the members of the security forces who went into Ljuboten village were risking their lives to do their duties, to protect the sovereignty of Macedonia, the --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic is on her feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The idea of investigating the actions of the security forces at Ljuboten was actually pretty offensive to you, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why would this be offensive? I don't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Because your colleagues in the security forces -- the suggestion was that -- or the suggestion would be that rather than doing their duty, risking their lives on that day, the suggestion would be that your colleagues in the security forces had actually done something very wrong. Didn't you find that suggestion difficult and offensive?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot understand you. Could you rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, to you as a career member of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, did you hear about allegations from groups like Human Rights Watch that members of the security forces had committed abuses in Ljuboten village?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were such allegations.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And didn't you find those allegations to be pretty offensive and an insult to the honour -- members of the police and members of the army?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were an attack on the honour and dignity of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because, I am convinced, that my colleagues carried out their work tasks and obligations in a professional manner. And because these accusations were checked, we checked these allegations, and I believe they were unfounded. From that point of view, I can see them as offensive.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Mr. Stojanovski, many members of the Ministry of Internal Affairs felt the same way, didn't they, that these allegations were quite offensive?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Someone was expressing lack of trust in the police. We were put in a position to prove the opposite, to be proving the opposite, which ultimately is fine. We have to be transparent in the work we do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But then the answer to my question would be yes, right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether things can be seen as black and white.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm not asking you to paint anything as black and white. Simply my question was this: Many members of the Ministry of Internal Affairs also felt that these allegations against the conduct of security forces in the village of Ljuboten were offensive, right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many members of the ministry thought. I can tell you what I was thinking.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And since the honour -- since the honour and the reputation of the police of Macedonia was at stake, the purpose of the investigation into the events at Ljuboten was to clear the honour and reputation of the police, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wrong. If you would like me to explain the purpose was to establish the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And is that why you so energetically provided assistance to members of the commission who were investigating the events in Ljuboten? And I use the word energetically in a very ironic sense.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I take note of your irony. I don't know by what right I have earned this. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm about to move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, before you do, Ms. Residovic had some matters she wished to raise, but it was at a fairly significant [Realtime transcript read in error "criminal"] point of cross-examination so I signalled to her to wait. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, you direct the proceedings, and I believe your decision was ultimately correct. However the entire series of questions posed by my learned friend was unclear to me regarding their relevancy. I wanted to ask why so many questions were being put to the witness which go to various opinions. However, if you were able to follow the thread of the questions being put, I have no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I didn't have the difficulty that you are mentioning at all, Ms. Residovic and it seemed to me that we were at a significant point in the cross-examination and it was important to allow it to reach its natural conclusion. Could I just mention that in line 29: 1, I had intended to say critical point rather than criminal point as the transcript would have me record it. Thank you. Now, Mr. Saxon you were signalling that you're about to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will then have the break and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, at page 9072 of the transcript - this was very early on in your direct examination - you were asked about an interview that you had with members of the Office of the Prosecutor, some years ago, and you were asked about the statement that -- a statement that was drafted at that time but ultimately not signed by you. And you explained to the Judges: "I thought there were misunderstandings with regards to the format in which the statement was to be taken. I believe that what I am saying needs to be entered while the investigators thought that they were to rephrase it, to state there what they understood from what I was saying." And you also explained that, further on: "There were misunderstandings related to certain facts, and I can't really remember that, after which they threatened me in the sense that they could indict me for certain issues and their conduct went outside of the boundaries of propriety. And this is why I decided to leave the room where the interview was conducted." Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we could show the witness what is tab 1 of the first Prosecution binder, please. And this is it Prosecution 65 ter 1150. And perhaps if we could show the witness, first -- the first page in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, we see here what is usually referred to as the cover page of a witness statement. And you see your name on this draft statement, don't you?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And are the details correct, as far as you can tell?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I can tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So we see there was one person interviewing you, Mr. Matti Raatikainen and an interpreter. We see that, right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. When you say "there were two of them," what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two investigators and a translator.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And now perhaps if you could turn to -- we have a Macedonian translation of this document. If you could turn to that, please. And if you could direct your attention, please, to paragraph 5 of the Macedonian version, so I think it would be on -- it would be on the next page that you're looking at now. And paragraph 5 tells this: "During the time I was the deputy of the criminal police of Skopje," that is the first half of 2000 to the summer of 2002, "my direct supervisor was the assistant minister for SVR Skopje, who, in the summer of 2001 was Mr. Zoran Efremov. Efremov reported to the head of public security, Mr. Goran Mitevski; and his superior was Mr. Ljube Boskoski, the minister of the interior. I was responsible for everything that had to do with preventing and investigating crime, like general crime, economic crime and drug-related crime in SVR Skopje." And then it says this: "If I had to issue orders that had to do with the area of operation and responsibility of Cair police station, I would do it through the head of OVR who, in 2001, was Mr. Ljube Krstevski. Depending on the case, the orders were issued either in writing or verbally, and the head of the OVR reported back in a similar manner, that is, if he had received a written order he normally also responded in writing." Have you followed me?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Isn't this what you told the investigators back in August of 2004?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this is the statement which I did not sign.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: My question is something different. I'm asking you if what I just read to you in paragraph 5 was what you told the investigators in August of 2004.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And what is different or incorrect in this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you followed my evidence and testimony, you would know what is different and what is identical.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir, but I need a more specific response, please.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I was not a deputy; I was an assistant. There was no reporting. I was not responsible for everything pertaining to crime, orders, the manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What about the orders? What about the orders or the manner of orders is incorrect?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the superior of OVR Cair was the head of SVR Skopje. If there had been an order, only Mr. Efremov was authorised to have issued such an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What if Mr. --

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The manner issued in written form or verbally does not correspond, because, as I explained, the verbal ones were supplemented with written ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if Mr. Efremov was not present in SVR Skopje, who would then issue a necessary order to a head of an OVR?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Efremov was present in SVR Skopje, only I believe he was absent at the end 2000, 2001 when he had a car accident and was hurt.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But you told us, I believe, during your cross-examination that there were times when simply Mr. Efremov was not physically at the SVR Skopje office, and in those times, matters were directed either to you or to Mr. Bliznakovski, right?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe this is misstating the evidence. The witness never said it was when Efremov was physically away from his office. The Prosecutor should refer back to the page of the transcript to see what the witness exactly had said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, yesterday I showed the witness a document that had a handwritten note on it saying, To Pero Stojan; and I asked the witness why -- in fact it was a document from April 2001 it was a plan or an addition to a plan from OVR Cair regarding the placement of check-points and I asked the witness why was this document directed to you? And the witness answered that there were certain times where, if Mr. Efremov, his boss, was not available in SVR Skopje, matters would be directed either to the witness or to Mr. Bliznakovski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Basically accurate in what you say, Mr. Saxon, that was not the initial effect of the evidence of the witness so there is something to be said for both Ms. Residovic's position and your own; but I'm sure this witness is capable of making clear where and if you should misrepresent his understanding of his position. So please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So if Mr. Efremov was not physically present in SVR Skopje at a given moment and an order needed to be issued to an OVR, who would issue such an order?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, in terms of the explanation for the document was different than what you claim; and, second, if Mr. Efremov was not physically present, he had a cell phone and he was always available.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you turn, please, to paragraph 6. Is there anything in paragraph 6 that is incorrect?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Above all, this paragraph is based or has as a starting point the presumption that SVR did not undertake any activities regarding the events in Ljuboten. If you followed my testimony, you would have known that SVR Skopje, in regards to this event, carried out the function of coordination.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, my question was simply is the contents of paragraph 6 correct. You can answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Well, all right. And how about paragraph 7? Actually, let's go back to paragraph 6, if you will. Didn't you testify that SVR Skopje did not undertake any activity, vis-a-vis the events in Ljuboten, that SVR Skopje was not involved?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Well, how was SVR Skopje then involved in the Ljuboten events?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I previously explained, on the 12th, on the day of the activities, assistance was requested by OVR Cair for public law and order, regarding what was happening at the check-points, and at the exits of the village of Ljuboten. Help was requested also for coordinating activities when preparing the criminal report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you take a look at paragraph 8, please, Mr. Stojanovski, it says: "I cannot remember whether I would have asked Mr. Krstevski or somebody else to attend a particular meeting in Ljubanci on the 10th of August, 2001. I probably have asked him to attend such a meeting, but I cannot remember any details. Neither do I remember whether he would have reported to me about what happened at the meeting." Isn't this what you told the investigators in August of 2004?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave my oath or declaration as a witness here, and what I said here is the truth. What is indicated here is an interpretation made by your investigators who believe me to be a member or participant in a joint criminal enterprise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you take a look at paragraph 10, please. It say: "When I am being asked whether I was contacted by Ljube Krstevski on Friday, 10 August 2001 or on Saturday, 11 August 2001, regarding a group of people demanding weapons from the Cair police station, I answer that this is the first time I hear about such a thing. I don't believe that Ljube Krstevski called me about this issue during that weekend, and I do believe that since this is a rather serious matter I would remember it." Isn't that what you told the investigators in August 2004?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that you showed that I had contacts with Mr. Ljube Krstevski.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm sure if you've answered my question. Is the contents -- do the contents of paragraph 10 reflect what you told the investigators in August 2004. Again, can you --

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And take a look at paragraph 11, please, which says: "When being asked whom Krstevski normally would report about this kind of an issue, I reply that normally he would report it to Efremov, myself, or the assistant minister." That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not agree with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So what is written here -- so you did not tell the investigator what is written here in paragraph 11. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could you turn to paragraph 14, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It will be on the next page in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Paragraph 14 begins: "Being asked whether I remember what was reported to me by my subordinates on the 12th of August, 2001, I reply that I cannot really remember whether somebody reported to me anything that day. As I have said earlier, SVR Skopje was not involved in the events in Ljuboten. When being asked if I knew anything about what was going on in Ljuboten, I remember that Ljube Krstevski informed me on the day, before the combat activities about the presence of the army of Macedonia in the area." Isn't that what you told the investigators in August 2001 [sic]?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Are you suggesting that the investigators made this information up and wrote it down?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I judge it by their assertion that I was a participant in a criminal enterprise, probably they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So it's your position that this information in paragraph 14 did not come from you, it was simply made up by the investigators and written down the way it was written. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Processed. So probably I said something, they probably processed it in their own way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And your suggestion is that the investigators processed it in their own way in order to try to bring criminal charges against you?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't judge their ideas at that time and their intentions. However, it is a fact that they believed me to be a participant in a joint criminal enterprise and probably they have serious facts in support to this. I am convinced of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, you see, Mr. Stojanovski, there is nothing in the sentences in paragraph 14 that would -- that I've read to you at least that would indicate that you were a participant in any crime or joint criminal enterprise. So I'm trying to understand why you think that these investigators somehow, in bad faith, made up these sentences and put them in this draft statement.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of the entire construction they made.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you turn, please, to the last page of the draft statement. Go toward paragraph 22, please. Paragraph 22 says: "What I have said above is everything I can say about what I know about what happened in Ljuboten and about what I know about the role of my superiors and the policemen under my command." And then there was a paragraph 23 that was written, but it has some slash marks through it in a black pen. But you can still see what the drafters wrote there. It says: "After this statement has been translated to me into English, I state that even though I speak and understand the English language, I will sign the statement only if it is in Macedonian. If there will be a Macedonian translation available, I will be happy to sign it." Have you followed me, Mr. Stojanovski?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And that's what you told the investigators at the time, isn't it, that you wanted -- if you were going to sign a statement, it had to be a statement written in the Macedonian language, right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said already, the interview ended in a bit of a different atmosphere and environment. With regards to the language, that was part of a previous conversation, not at the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But it is what you told the investigators, that you would not sign a statement unless the statement was written in the Macedonian language, right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked to have a statement in the Macedonian language as well. And with regards to negotiations as to whether to sign, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you refused to sign this statement because it was drafted in English rather than in the Macedonian language, right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are playing with my words. I explained before why I did not sign this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, I'm not playing with anything. And I'd like an answer to my question. You can just answer yes or no, if you'd like.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And it's true, isn't it, that back in 2004 when you spoke with OTP investigators, and even during your testimony here in this courtroom that have you been trying to distance yourself from the preparations for the attack on the village of Ljuboten that occurred on Sunday, 12th of August. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you like to explain this? I tried to distance myself?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That you are trying to hide your own involvement in the preparations for the attack on the village of Ljuboten that occurred on Sunday, 12th of August, 2001. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's true, isn't it, that you witnessed the beating of ethnic Albanian civilians by police officers at OVR Cair on the afternoon of 12 August 2001, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not like that at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's true, isn't it, Mr. Stojanovski, that you helped to ensure that the group of men that were led into the village of Ljuboten by Johan Tarculovski were armed and given uniforms and transportation at OVR Cair. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is again not true, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's true, Mr. Stojanovski, that you directed your subordinates, such as Ljube Krstevski, to assist Johan Tarculovski and the group of men who he would eventually lead into Ljuboten. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is completely untrue. I don't know Mr. Johan Tarculovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it's also true, isn't it, that during the weekend of 10 to 12 August you kept your superiors informed about the planning and preparations for the attack on Ljuboten. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is absolutely not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And subsequent to the events in and around Ljuboten in August 2001, you took no genuine measures to investigate any of the crimes that occurred there. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is again incorrect, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, before I move on to my cross-examination [as interpreted], my re-direct, I just wanted to react on behalf of the Defence. It is something that had to do with my learned friend's questions just before the break. I don't believe those questions were appropriate. You told us at the outset of these proceedings that witnesses should not be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic, you raised a concern before the break. It was dealt with. We don't want the matter going over again.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, maybe there is a misunderstanding. I wanted to react to the last series of questions, but thank you for your warning. In any case, I won't address the issue anymore and I will respect your decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, during my learned friend's cross-examination, you will remember that you were asked a question as to whether you can confirm what activities were undertaken by your colleague Ljupco Bliznakovski, on the 11th of August. Do you remember that question?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Some of the questions regards that topic had to do with whether it would be normal under the given circumstances that an order would be issued to strengthen the check-points in the area of Cair municipality, in particular around Ljuboten village. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was asked that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: During examination-in-chief, you were shown a number of orders issued at the police stations in Cair and Mirkovci stipulating the number of persons that were manning the check-points on the 12th of August, 2001. Did you in any of the orders notice the -- any mention of the notion of re-enforcing the check-points?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the orders that I saw, I did not notice anything of the sort.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, do you recall having had a conversation with my learned friend the Prosecutor concerning your statement. It was just mentioned that you told the head of the Cair OVR that he was to inform the minister, once the minister is in the area, and you explained that oral reporting or debriefing is not a standard procedure with the police. Do you remember having discussed that with my learned friend?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember having discussed that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In line 12, it says oral reporting whereas I said that the minister was supposed to be informed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor showed you numerous Official Notes as well as operative information and other types of informing used by the police. Do you remember having been shown that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was showing me operative information and Official Notes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You agreed that it was one of the ways of passing on information in the police.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is one of the ways.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also explained that it had nothing to do with debriefings or oral reports that you discussed previously?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tried to.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to what you said, that reporting orally is not a way of passing on information in the police --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, there seems to be some confusion concerning interpretation. I see that every time I say "Raport" it is being translated as reporting orally or passing on information orally. Maybe there is no better way to put it in another language, but I will try to clarify what the witness wanted to say in a different way.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, "Raport" in its military sense, and that is what you discussed, has something to do with the contents of information, or with a strictly prescribed procedure followed by the military in order to inform superiors?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Having in mind that in 1980 I served my military service, and as far as I can remember, it was a procedure, so ...

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All information on Official Notes shown to you by the Prosecutor, do these have anything to do with this strict way of reporting in the military, which we referred to as "raport"?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are two completely different concepts.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall having been asked by the Prosecutor about the possibility at the institute for forensic medicine to gather information of sorts? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we spoke to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you to -- the third set of documents, Defence documents, tab 168. It is P49004, under seal. Can you see the document?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Dragan Nikolovski, the investigative judge, was sent to the institute for forensic medicine, and he requested the notes of autopsy. When you look at the document, in your experience is it the only way for the institute to forward its findings --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What is the point of your objection, Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That we are receiving now a very question. Look at the document, in your experience, is it the only way for the institute to forward its findings. That is clearly a question that suggests the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Perhaps you could rephrase it, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, have a look at the document. What does it mean to you?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is a document produced by the investigating department of the Basic Court Skopje II, a request sent to the forensic medicine and criminology institute in Skopje, through which the institute is requested to submit the autopsy protocol from the post-mortem of Atulla Qaili.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can such a request be made by the police to the institute?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that during the previous discussions we stated that this is the exclusive competence of the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please have a look at the other binder you have, tab 128. It is Exhibit P54030, under seal. Do you have the document before you?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what it is?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The investigating judge, Velce Pancevski, requested information from the forensic medicine institute, Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What person, Bara ...
