utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He requested documents on the person Atulla Qaili.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, what does this exhibit point to?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this corroborate what had I stated before, that the investigating judge is the one who has the official communication and requests things from the forensic medicine institute.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your third binder, have a look at tab 177. It is a 65 ter document, 1D227. Before that, Mr. Stojanovski, tell me this: Do you know who Jovan Serafimovski is?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that he was a deputy public prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is a statement given by Jovan Serafimovski, deputy of the basic public prosecutor in Skopje gave to the investigators of this Tribunal. I wanted to refer to certain paragraphs of the statement. In paragraph 10, which is to be found on page 4, we can see: [In English] "... Qaili it will referred to under number 7 I was not there on 14 August 2001 that the accused Qaili Atulla was already dead. I learned about the death of Atulla Qaili by receiving a written information from the investigative Judge Velce Pancevski. It was my obligation to find out of the cause of death of Atulla Qaili. We learned that he was injured during a clash with the Macedonian security forces in Ljuboten. I was informed from the media that police and army were in Ljuboten. I don't know which unit of the police and army were involved. I didn't know the unit or name of the police or army officers who were directly involved in the death of Atulla Qaili. I did not try to find out who was involved in the death of Atulla Qaili, because I was told that a lot of security forces were involved in this events. In the Official Note to the police, it was mentioned that the security forces were active in Ljuboten. That was all the information about the events that we received." [Interpretation] Let us look at paragraph 13, which mentions the same person [in English] "... Atulla Qaili, I knew the two other persons who were arrested in Ljuboten were hospitalised together with Atulla Qaili. I only remember that these two accused were in the city hospital. I knew this because I read about this in the notes of the questioning which are part of the files. I can't recall the name of these two persons, although normally the investigative judge has an obligation to ascertain the cause of the injuries, as I explained early, I learned that these persons were injured during the clashes with the Macedonian security forces. It was a war situation and at that time I did not even think about trying to learn the cause of these injuries." [Interpretation] In paragraph 14, the Prosecutor Serafimovski states --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please read slowly and make pauses when switching between different languages, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] If this document was produced by the investigative judge, then I have never been informed from him about this. In reference to the death of Atulla Qaili, I only learned about the injuries from the death certificate. I think the autopsy was initialised by the investigative judge, Velce Pancevski. Normally, it would be my obligation as a deputy public prosecutor to ask for an autopsy. If I had known that the person was dead, when I was filed the question for an investigation, I would have requested the autopsy. But in the case of Atulla Qaili, it was the investigative judge." [Interpretation] Mr. Stojanovski, you heard what the Prosecutor Serafimovski said. To what extent does this statement by the Prosecutor Serafimovski when he says that he -- his obligation or, rather the obligation of the investigative judge, to what extent is it correct, in keeping with the laws that were in place in Macedonia and according to your experience.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that we discussed something similar previously, as well with regards to the autopsy and exhumation, and I believe that we said then, or, actually, I said that as far as I know, to undertake such actions the investigating judge has the competence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Concerning the part of the statement by Mr. Serafimovski, in which he says that when he learned about his obligation to undertake measures, does that differ from your testimony or does it corroborate your actual testimony before this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it corroborates it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will ask you to have a look at the Prosecutor's binder, tab 105. It is document -- I can't see exactly what the exhibit number would be, but it is an Official Note, number 1090.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the ERN numbers in Macedonian and English slowly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can see it is P37, under seal, on the list.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, do you recall being shown this document by the Prosecutor as well? I apologise, maybe it wasn't. You were shown --

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was not shown.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were shown P105. I don't know where it is in the binder, but could we please have that placed on the screen. You remember being shown this document. We discussed it at length whereby we said that the title, Official Note, was translated as operative information. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the counsel to pause before starting a new question. Would the counsel please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm being told that this is tab 79 in the Prosecutor's binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question was whether you recall being shown this document.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were shown some additional documents and you were asked whether you told the commission or other MVR members that they should talk to some other people that were shown this document as well. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that they knew what their job was and that they are more familiar with it than you are. Am I interpreting that correctly?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Regarding that, I have the following questions for you, Mr. Stojanovski. Those members of commissions or of the MVR, could they take over the responsibility of the competent organs within the MVR or the SVR which were tasked or duty-bound to investigate any such event, including the one in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This could not happen.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you, upon their request, provide all of the documents had you at your disposal and did you hide some of the documents?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I handed over all documents to the committee, and I organised that these documents be available to the analytics department of the SVR Skopje as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As the liaison person with the Cair OVR, since you were tasked with that by Mr. Efremov, your superior, did you also make sure that the Cair OVR should made available all information they had at their disposal?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is a leading question on a very critical point. Perhaps it could be rephrased.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, you said that the head of the VR [as interpreted] in Skopje, on the 13th, told you to serve as liaison between the commission and the organs of the Ministry of Interior and the OVR Cair. Did you accept that duty and did you execute those tasks?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I executed it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to that and the requests sent to you by the Ministry of Interior, were any measures undertaken by which those people would be enabled to reach the Cair OVR?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke to several heads, chiefs, and I informed them of their duty to cooperate with the commission.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did any of the heads and persons you talked to say that they refused to provide documents or that they refused to discuss the event?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It happened once only.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us when?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do not see how this question falls within the remit of cross-examination, and so that's why I'm objecting to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think the implementations of your cross-examination may be wider than you are imagining. I wouldn't stop Ms. Residovic at this point.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question was, on what occasion did it happen that someone or that one person refused to provide documents?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The head of the OVR Cair did not want to cooperate with Mrs. Galeva.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, in your previous answers, you said that based on the documents you received, you were unable to conclude that some policemen overstepped or abused their authority. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you go through the documents carefully?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I reviewed them and, as I explained to the Prosecutor, I don't how willing he was to understand what I was saying, it was important for the ministry to ascertain the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Concerning your basic task, which was to establish the truth, based on any of the documents, were you able to confirm the suspicions raised and prevailing among the public concerning the behaviour of the police?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't confirm such statements or -- how should I say? That were presented in the media at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were shown a document by the Prosecutor. Is it 1D183, which is tab 45 in the second Defence binder, and you were asked some questions about it. Do you recall this document?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You gave answers to both me and my learned friend Mr. Saxon, whereby you said that you believed the document was sent to you.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I recall, you said that it is possible that it found its way to you because on that day you may have been at the headquarters at the SVR. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the counsel and witness to avoid overlapping.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, there is a handwritten note for deputy Pero Stojan, which you said probably meant it was for you. Just below it, the date says the 15th of April, 2002. In addition to the fact that you may have been given this document at the time it was drafted, can you tell us why such a document would be sent to you on the 15th of April, 2002?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only explanation that I could remember now would be that it was probably upon a request by the commission.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do I understand correctly, that you were trying to get by certain information throughout that period?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a continuous process.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let us have a look at tab 99. I believe it is a Prosecution exhibit. It is -- no, it is 1D189. Do you recall being shown this document by the Prosecutor? You also provided certain answers in relation to the document. It is in the second Prosecution binder. You agreed with the Prosecutor that the information on the allegedly killed in the village of Ljuboten is important.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I stated that it was useful.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you also said that it is incomplete, since it also contained certain information which, at the time, you already knew was incorrect. For instance, when it is stated that the people were buried the same day they were killed.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also provided answers concerning the way information is checked in order to establish whether a crime had been committed. Can you tell me whether this information was sufficient to corroborate the suspicion that there was a crime committed?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you this: On the day you attempted to carry on an on-site investigation, did you also receive information regarding the persons buried?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe this was on the 14th when we were informed that the persons were buried. It was an information received through the conversations which the head of OVR Cair, Krstevski; head of SVR, Efremov of SVR Skopje, Efremov and MP Etemi had.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, do you remember being shown some information concerning a person from Skopje. That person provided information concerning Cair.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that there was such an information, but if I could see it, it would be better for me. The person was -- I think this was person was not from Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So as not to waste any time in trying to find that information, I would kindly ask you to look at tab 148, which is in the second Defence binder. It is P104. P104. N005- --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not get the ERN number. It is in Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said a minute ago that the information you just saw was insufficient for you to be able to address the issue of a suspicion of crime being committed. You were told by the Prosecutor that that note was compiled by Dejan Blazevski?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who drafted this note, the one before you?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Dejan Blazevski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We have already seen this note. Does it contain sufficient relevant data, which may be used to ascertain whether those people were killed or died in the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only on the basis of this information, no, there was no such information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have a look at the previous note. It is tab 147. Exhibit 1D190. During examination-in-chief, that note was shown to you as well. It is page 1D47351 in the Macedonian; and in the English it is 1D4753.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see in this report of the Cair OVR that they are actually providing a response to the Basic Court and its investigative judge. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you also see from the document that it quotes the court decision, or, rather, a request that was sent by the court in order to perform their tasks?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the court had submit a request.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please have a look at another document, which is tab 146. It is 1D47, page 1D1949 in the Macedonian and 1590 in the English.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document compiled by the investigative judge used by the OVR Cair in their response.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the second paragraph the court requests: "In order to undertake these investigation actions, it is necessary on your part to gather some additional reports and data, with the aim of determining the identity of these persons, the location of the graves where the corpses were buried, the time of burial, obtaining statements from the persons who performed the burial, statements of family members of the buried as well as other data and reports and written material." Is this what the court requested?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You worked for a number of years with the crime squad. According to what you know, it is one of the necessary prerequisites for a court to initialise an autopsy?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is usual beforehand to have the necessary information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The note shown to you by the Prosecutor, in which we have first and last names of persons with the incorrect date of burial, that note in itself, did it suffice to answer any of the questions or parts of the request made by the court?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we could not rely on this information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the third Defence binder, you -- could you please have a look at tab 156. It is exhibit P490034, under seal.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We can see that it was created on the 5th of February, 2002.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And we have some text in English. Based on that, we can conclude that these are the actual burial locations. Could the police obtain this information in any way during 2001 and 2002?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it could not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have a look at tab 158. It is Exhibit P5555, under seal. Again, we have a drawing displaying the graves of the victims of the 12th of August with their names, and the title is in English. The police, with all the efforts you invested in order to investigate, were you able to obtain this information?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think I explained previously that we did not have cooperation with the local population. Such cooperation was refused.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have a look at tab 159. It is Exhibit P5528, under seal. In his request, Judge Nikolovski requested that interviews be carried out with the members of the families of those allegedly killed.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think this was in connection with the identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this document, which was compiled on the 21st of March, 2002, Osman Ramadani gave a statement to the investigative judge. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the judge had requested that he be given statements by those people initially.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have a look at the next page of the document.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the last paragraph it says: "At the hearing the deputy of the basic public prosecutor's office Cakic was present. Investigative Judge Bekir Shahini in addition to Dragan Nikolovski, the representative from the municipality community, Ljuboten Kenan Salievski, as well as representatives of The Hague Tribunal Andrzej Szydlik, and Ali Nakija from The Hague Tribunal." Mr. Stojanovski, you testified about this earlier, was it possible to address the issue or to answer the question of what had actually happened without having any statements of family members who could tell you something about those killed?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: From what I have just said, it is clear that no police representatives were there.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is the police ever present during an interview conducted by a judge in -- in a court building?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it clear from what I read to you that the interview of this person, and this was a family member of one of the deceased, is it clear that we -- that who was present were actually some village representatives and people from The Hague Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since you are fully familiar with the situation at the time, was it possible to get by some real true information based on which what could make educated guesses or conclusions as to what happened, based on the statements given and the fate of the people killed?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could the police make it possible for the court to have those people appear before the court and give statements, since the court requested so?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, to shorten this part of my examination, I just wanted to say that it is identical to P5557 under seal which is in tab 60; and then exhibit P5521, under seal, tab 161; P5525, under seal, tab 162.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have a look at tab 120 in the second Defence binder. It is 1D9. Tab 120. This document is also under seal. The page is 1D0040. We have it in English only. Mr. Stojanovski, we have here investigator's notes, the purpose of which was to note the meeting with the representatives of the families of the deceased from Ljuboten, the Republic of Macedonia, in order to discuss the operational plan for the exhumation at the cemetery at the village of Ljuboten. The meeting was held on the 8th of March, Friday, at 10.30. You can see those present. On behalf of the village, there were three people. Then you can see who the representatives of the families under items 1 through 8. Then we have the representatives of the international community, Mathias Elck of the OSCE, and Valentine Guileri of the OSCE as well as Demeri-Shaipi, of the same organisation interpreter. On behalf of the international Tribunal, we have Howard Tucker investigator and Andzrey Sydlic operations officer in the office in Skopje. Is it all visible from the first page?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are investigator's notes with a degree of confidentiality.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have a look at page 2. I will read out the last paragraph [In English] ... "There was initial resistance by the spokesperson of the crisis committee, Mr. Saliu Kenan about the involvement of the Republic of Macedonia agency. Feelings were obviously running high and there was talk of non-cooperation by the villages. However, after further discussion, they all greed their support for the investigation." [Interpretation] Mr. Stojanovski, these investigator's notes stating the fact that the villagers expressed a lack of trust in all Macedonian agencies and state bodies and refused to cooperate, was it drafted in March 2002 and does it confirm what you know of the events at the time confirming that the police was actually unable to get by information?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only the police. All institutions of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have a look at the next page. It is 1D1142. The fourth line from the bottom -- not line, excuse me, paragraph. It says [in English] ..."Anyway, the bodies remaining in storage at the institute until the process is completed was not acceptable to the families of the deceased. They still carry a huge mistrust of anything Macedonian." [Interpretation] Does this assertion, on the part of The Hague Tribunal investigator, confirm your knowledge as to the police being unable to combine information?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a correct assertion.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I note the time. However, I have quite a few questions left. I don't know whether we can continue with the witness or ... I covered the questions raised today. However, we also have yesterday's cross-examination, and I will have some questions about that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We must adjourn now, because of the time. We will resume tomorrow at 9.00, in the anticipation that you will finish in the course of the first session tomorrow. We will be able to resume our normal programme with the next witness, and we'll sit through until 1.45 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 14th day of February, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 12.34 p.m.,
